_comment: Parts you can't buy: each one is somewhere in the city (scripts/world/found_part.gd). `near` is a barn find (barn:<car id>), a job site (site:<id>), a photo spot (photo:<id>) from data/world/places.json, or a beach, fishing spot or landmark from the map (poi:<id>, index.json "pois"); `offset` is metres east, up and south of it; optional `yaw` turns it (wheels lean toward their local -X); `on_foot` means stopping the car next to it doesn't take it, you have to walk up to it. `rumour` shows in the phone's Leads tab until it's found. A part only turns up once you own a car it fits. Stop next to it or walk up to it to take it home.

parts.rumour: The warehouse on Royal Street had a set of old magnesium wheels leaning by the roller door.
Someone left an Abarth tailpipe on the bench of a Kensington shed.
There's a rack and an old single-fin out the back of the Cottesloe surf club. Nobody's claimed it.
A pair of chrome spotlights is sitting on the kerb along Mounts Bay Road in Crawley.
One of the old blokes who fishes the North Mole turned a gear knob out of a brass bollard cap. He left it by the car park for whoever wants it.
The antique shop in Guildford put a cream steering wheel out on the grass by the side street. A sign says free to a good home.
Someone left a roof basket with an old esky in it at the Trigg Beach car park. It's been there all week.
There's an old black-and-white number plate propped against the wall by the Station Street Markets in Subiaco.
